directAnswer: You can reset Windows while keeping your files by using the 'Reset this PC' feature in the settings. This option reinstalls Windows without affecting your personal files.
summary: Resetting Windows can help resolve issues while preserving your personal files. Follow the steps below to perform this operation safely.

sections.heading: What is Resetting Windows?
sections.body: Resetting Windows reinstalls the operating system, removing apps and settings that may be causing issues, while giving you the option to keep your personal files intact.

sections.heading: When to Reset Windows
sections.body: Consider resetting Windows if your computer is slow, experiencing frequent crashes, or if you want to resolve persistent software issues without a full reinstall.

steps.title: Open Settings
steps.detail: Click on the Start menu and select 'Settings' (gear icon).

steps.title: Navigate to Recovery
steps.detail: In the Settings window, select 'Update & Security', then click on 'Recovery' in the left sidebar.

steps.title: Start the Reset Process
steps.detail: Under 'Reset this PC', click the 'Get started' button.

steps.title: Choose to Keep Files
steps.detail: Select the option 'Keep my files' when prompted to choose how to reset.

faqs.question: Will resetting Windows delete my installed programs?
faqs.answer: Yes, resetting Windows will remove installed applications, but your personal files will remain.

faqs.question: Can I back up my files before resetting?
faqs.answer: It's always a good idea to back up your files to an external drive or cloud storage before performing a reset.

faqs.question: What happens to my settings after the reset?
faqs.answer: All system settings will be restored to their defaults, and you'll need to reconfigure them after the reset.

caveats: While your personal files should remain intact, there is always a risk of data loss, so backing up important files is recommended.
